scope: Proposition 5.1 of the manuscript “A nondegenerate counterexample to the Morse-number Arnold bound” (preprints/A-nondegenerate-counterexample-to-the-Morse-number-Arnold-bound-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 347 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f7980995971b08df), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (X, ωX) be a closed connected symplectic four-manifold. Write (u, v) ∈ R4 × R4 and set Q(u, v) = |v|2 − |u|2 2 , r2 = |u|2 + |v|2 . Suppose that F : X × R8 → R is a smooth Morse function such that F = Q whenever r ≥ 3, and let N = # Crit(F). Let σ be the standard area form of total area 4π on the unit sphere. For every λ > 25/2, the closed symplectic manifold (M, ωM ) =  X × (S2 )4 , ωX + λ 4 X j=1 σj   admits a Hamiltonian H ∈ C∞((R/Z) × M, R) such that every fixed point of ϕ1 H is nondegen- erate, every loop t 7→ ϕt H(p) based at a fixed point p is contractible in M, and # Fix0(ϕ1 H; H) = # Fix(ϕ1 H) = 16N. Here σj denotes the pullback of σ from the jth sphere, and Hamiltonian vector fields satisfy ωM (XH, ·) = dH.
